PINOW DILG Legal Opinion No. 16, S. 2013 08 MAY 2013 MR. JONATHAN Y. PEPITO HRMO 111 Tuburan, Cebu Dear Mr. Pepito: This refers to your 02 January 2013 letter which requests the Department's legal opinion on whether the former staff of deceased Vice Governor Sanchez may claim their overtime pay withheld by Cebu Governor Gwendolyn F. Garcia based on the decision rendered by the Office of the President (OP) in Hon. Gregorio G. Sanchez, Jr. vs. Hon. Gwendolyn E Garcia, O.P. Case No. 104<-504. The following are the Department's comments relative to the above issue: Scope of the Office of the President's urisdiction in Administrative Disci lina Cases The Office of the President's (OP) jurisdiction in administrative disciplinary cases against covered elective local officials only extends to the determination of the latter's culpability for acts or omissions imputed against them based on the grounds enumerated under Section 60 of Republic Act No. 7160. The OP'S adjudicatory power does extend to the determination of the complainant's entitlement to claims for damages and other monetary claims arising from the imputed acts or omissions. Whether the former staff of Vice Governor Sanchez ma claim their overtime a based on the Office of the President's Pecision in O.P. CaseNo. IO-K-504 'The factual findings of administrative officials and agencies that have acquired expertise in the performance of their official duties and the exercise of their primary jurisdiction are generally accorded not only respect but, at times, even finality if such findings are supported by substantial evidence. Hence, the administrative agency's factual findings of the respondent's culpability for the imputed acts or omissions may be used as basis to support claims arising therefrom by the complainant or other affected individuals. However, the administrative agency's Decision raquinod v. Court of Appeals, G.R. No. 154654, 14 September 2007, 533 SCRA 403. It's more fun in the Phil

does not per se automatically entitle the complainant or other affected individuals to their claims as the same necessitates the filing of an appropriate request/petition before the proper authority. In the case of the Office of the President's (OP) Decision in O.P. Case No. IO-K-504, no judgment was rendered on Governor Garcia's culpability for grave abuse of discretion on the matter of withholding the overtime pay of the personnel of the Office of the Governor in the absence of any evidence to support the allegations and the lack of pertinent findings by the investigating authority, viz: "As to the other acts complained of,' i.e. stopping the publication of the Legislative Gavel and non-payment of the honoraria of the publication staff,' and; withholding of overtime pay of the personnel of the Office of' the Vice- Governor, the absence of any evidence to support the allegations and the lack of pertinent findings by the investigating authorit.v, constrains this Office from making any iudgment on the same. " In view of the foregoing, we advise you to file your claim for overtime pay before the proper office in the Provincial Governrnent of Cebu to determine your entitlement thereto subject to pertinent Civil Service Commission (CSC) rules and the Guidelines and Procedures on Overtime Services issued by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM). Very truly yours, ESUS B. Director cc OQ EIV RD ANANIAS M. VILLACORTA DILG-Region VII Sudlon, Lahiug, Cebu City
